questions.scenario: You are making instant noodles for your friends. What is your cooking style?

options.text: I add my own secret masalas, cheese, and veggies to create a totally new flavor.
I measure the water perfectly and boil it for exactly 2 minutes so it's not soggy.
I serve it in special deep bowls so it stays hot longer and doesn't spill.
I taste the broth three times while cooking to make sure the salt and spice levels are perfect.

questions.scenario: You are buying a bag of chips from the local store. What do you notice first?

options.text: The 'New Flavor!' tag and wondering how they made it taste like tandoori pizza.
The expiry date and checking if the bag is sealed properly with no air leaks.
How the bag is designed with foil inside to protect the chips from breaking.
Imagining the crunch, smell, and exact taste of the chips before I even open them.

questions.scenario: Your science teacher asks you to do a chemistry lab experiment. How do you approach it?

options.text: I mix extra chemicals just to see what kind of crazy reaction happens.
I follow the manual line by line to get the exact, perfect result safely.
I build a cool, stable stand to hold the test tubes so they don't tip over.
I observe the tiny color changes and smells really closely to note down details.

questions.scenario: You are packing your bag for a 3-day school trip. What is your priority?

options.text: Packing unique, homemade snacks that no one else has tried before.
Double-checking my checklist to ensure I haven't forgotten anything important.
Fitting everything perfectly using space-saving pouches so nothing gets crushed.
Making sure I have my favorite playlist and comfortable clothes to enjoy the vibe.

questions.scenario: You order a fancy dessert at a restaurant. When it arrives, you...

options.text: Wonder what culinary process made the sauce so thick, glossy, and unique.
Check if the plate is clean and if the presentation matches the picture on the menu.
Notice the structural design of the chocolate dome melting over the cake.
Close your eyes on the first bite to deeply analyze the mix of sweet, salty, and crunchy.

questions.scenario: What is your biggest pet peeve (annoyance) when eating street food?

options.text: When the food is boring and tastes exactly like everything else on the street.
When the vendor handles the food with dirty hands or uses unhygienic water.
When the flimsy paper plate bends and drops the food onto my shoes.
When the texture is weird—like when something that should be crispy gets soggy.

questions.scenario: Your class is doing a group project to build a model volcano. What is your role?

options.text: Figuring out the baking soda and vinegar mixture to make the biggest, most colorful eruption.
Proofreading the final science report to make sure there are zero mistakes.
Designing the physical structure of the volcano so it's strong and doesn't leak.
Painting it and adding fine textures so it looks and feels incredibly realistic.

questions.scenario: If you were stranded on an island, what survival skill would you rely on?

options.text: Mixing different wild plants to discover what is safe and nutritious to eat.
Creating a strict daily schedule for rationing our limited food and water.
Building strong, sealed containers out of bamboo to store rainwater.
Trusting my sharp senses to smell out fresh water or spot hidden fruits.

questions.scenario: If you could invent a new futuristic product, what would it be?

options.text: A chewing gum that changes flavor from a main course meal to dessert.
A pocket scanner that instantly tells you if food has bacteria or has gone bad.
A 100% edible water bottle that leaves zero plastic waste behind.
A virtual reality headset that perfectly recreates the smell and taste of your favorite memories.

questions.scenario: What kind of YouTube video are you most likely to watch at night?

options.text: A satisfying video of a chef making weird food combinations that actually work.
A deep dive into how fast-food chains keep their burgers exactly the same globally.
An engineering video on how aluminum soda cans are perfectly designed to hold pressure.
A food reviewer describing a massive $500 gourmet meal in extreme, mouth-watering detail.

Food_Scientist.title: Food Scientist / Product Developer
Food_Scientist.primary_match_text: You are wildly creative and love experimenting. You enjoy mixing things together to create something entirely new and aren't afraid to break the rules.
Food_Scientist.day_in_the_life: Working in a high-tech kitchen lab, mixing ingredients to create the next viral snack flavor, and researching plant-based meat alternatives.
Food_Scientist.alternative_match_text: Since you love experimenting and creating, developing new food products or recipes is a fantastic backup plan for your creative energy.
Food_Scientist.roadmap: Take Science (PCB or PCM) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Tech or B.Sc in Food Technology, Food Science, or Nutrition.

Quality_Assurance_Manager.title: Food Safety & Quality Assurance Manager
Quality_Assurance_Manager.primary_match_text: You have a sharp eye for detail and love perfection. You believe in rules, safety, and making sure everything works exactly as it is supposed to.
Quality_Assurance_Manager.day_in_the_life: Testing food samples for bacteria, inspecting massive food factories for hygiene, and ensuring that every single chocolate bar tastes and looks identical.
Quality_Assurance_Manager.alternative_match_text: Because you are detail-oriented and strict about quality, managing safety standards in the food or medical industry is a highly respected path.
Quality_Assurance_Manager.roadmap: Take Science (PCB or PCM) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Sc in Microbiology, Food Science, or a B.Tech in Food Technology.

Food_Packaging_Engineer.title: Food Packaging Technologist
Food_Packaging_Engineer.primary_match_text: You are a practical problem solver. You think about how things are built, how to protect them, and how to make designs smarter and more eco-friendly.
Food_Packaging_Engineer.day_in_the_life: Designing biodegradable wrappers that keep chips crispy for months, or engineering smart bottles that change color when milk goes bad.
Food_Packaging_Engineer.alternative_match_text: With your structural and practical mindset, designing packaging for food, electronics, or medical supplies is a highly paid and creative engineering route.
Food_Packaging_Engineer.roadmap: Take Science (PCM) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Tech in Packaging Technology, Materials Science, or Mechanical Engineering.

Sensory_Evaluator.title: Sensory Scientist / Flavor Expert
Sensory_Evaluator.primary_match_text: You are highly perceptive and tuned into your senses. You notice the tiny details in taste, smell, and texture that everyone else completely misses.
Sensory_Evaluator.day_in_the_life: Conducting blind taste tests, advising companies on whether a new soft drink is 'too fizzy,' and legally protecting famous secret flavor recipes.
Sensory_Evaluator.alternative_match_text: Because you have incredibly sharp senses and observation skills, analyzing flavors for the food, perfume, or beverage industry is a rare and exciting career.
Sensory_Evaluator.roadmap: Take Science (PCB) or Home Science in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Sc in Food Science or Chemistry, and specialize in Sensory Science or Flavor Chemistry.
